cards.note: The Amazon area is very distinct. It is fairly flat, and contains many of these trees with white bark (Cordia trichotoma), and oil palms.

These fences mostly found in the province of Manabí, located along the central-northwest of Ecuador.

*NOTE These fences can be found occasionally in other parts of the country. *
Banana plantations are most commonly found in the southwestern part of the country.
Cactus can be seen growing exclusively near the coast between Manta and Salinas.
Street signs differ from city to city - see the graphic.

If you see corn, you're west of the Andes.

The biggest corn production areas are Manabí and Los Ríos, but you can also find corn fields in Guayas and Loja.
The E-40 between Salinas and Guayaquil is one of the only divided highways in Ecuador, and the only one in the dry area near the southwestern coast.
There's a faint black smudge on the Google camera lens along the E-45 highway, all the way from Macas up north to Santa Clara.
As opposed to a normal Ecuador chevron that has four bolts on each side, the E487 road north from the city of Cumandá has only one bolt in the middle of the chevron.
The province of Esmeraldas can look similar to the Amazon region, but it is significantly hillier.
In the northeast of Ecuador you can find metal pipes along some of the roads.
This extremely dry landscape is only found in the coastal region between Guayaquil and Manta.
The flattest region is located around the city of Guayaquil.

Generation 4 cannot be found in the north-west and in the south-east (never in Esmeraldas).

*NOTE The whole truck is not always visible. *
In urban areas, you can commonly pavement consisting of hexagonal tiles.

The Google car antenna has two distinct variations:

The “high” antenna (purple), where the wire around the antenna is entirely above the halfway line of the antenna.

And the “low” antenna (blue) where the majority of the wire is below the halfway point of the line, and there can be a small bit poking up at the very top.

This is most useful when you have the high antenna, since it will always be in the northern half of the country.
Electricity poles with oval, see-through holes are most common in Loja province. They are occasionally found in neighbouring provinces.
On Northern chevrons, the bolts are positioned closer to the upper and lower edges, whereas on basic Ecuador chevrons, they are aligned closer to the center.

The vast majority of Ecuador's oil palm plantations are located in the northwest.

Some plantations are also found in the Amazon region.

In Ecuador, taxis feature orange license plates with red and white stickers on the side *NOTE similar stickers are used in Peru, but without the orange license plate. *

Other commercial vehicles, such as buses and freight vehicles, also use orange license plates.

cards.a: Semi arid area with pine trees
cards.note: The province of Chimborazo is semi-arid, and has an abundance of pine trees.

The southern regions have many winding mountain roads and exposed brownish red dirt.

The central provinces can have similar roads, but the exposed dirt will usually not be found in these areas.

Taxis in Ecuador are very common, and the first letter on each taxi can be used to determine the province you are in. The first letter of the taxi and the first letter of the province name are often the same.

NOTE: This letter will also appear as the first letter on ordinary licence plates respectively in each region. Beware that the letter P, as the letter for Pichincha (the region containing Quito), shows up occasionally in several regions.

“Aussie bollards” have a rectangular reflector on the front. Unlike actual Australian bollards, they are usually round. The most common type is the thin Aussie bollard, which is mostly found in the far south, with some clusters further north.

A tree-lined median divides E40 across the sections near the town of Guayaquil - see the map.

Note: on rare occasions in other parts of Ecuador.

The roads and hills in the province of Cotopaxi feature dark volcanic soil.

The region is often called "Avenue of the Volcanoes".
Visible water smudge on the Google car lens. You can find this on these roads: E30, E382, E20 & E38.
If you're driving through Guayas, you'll notice the guardrails stand out—they're painted in a distinct black-and-yellow pattern rather than the standard metallic silver or plain yellow.
